column3: “From after him” is rendered “from pursuing him.”
“To his innocence” is rendered “at random,” and “the camp” as “the fight”; NASB adds “severely.”
“The battle went up” is rendered “the battle raged,” and “was placed” as “was propped up.”
“When the sun went” is rendered “close to sunset.”
NASB puts the clause about the harlots in parentheses and supplies “there.”
MT 22:47. “Cult prostitutes” is rendered “sodomites,” and “destroyed” as “expelled.”
MT 22:49. The Hebrew reads “made” (written text “ten ships”); NASB keeps “made ships.”
